subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: The soil profile above the water table consists of which zones, from top to bottom?
options: Saturated zone, capillary fringe, vadose zone (unsaturated). Roots in vadose
Only the saturated zone that lies beneath the water table surface level
Only the vadose zone that lies between the land surface and the water table surface below
Only the capillary fringe that overlies the regional water table surface
solution: Vadose zone: moisture content < porosity. Infiltration, evapotranspiration, interflow.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: How do the minerals chlorite and biotite differ from each other in thin section?
options: Chlorite: anomalous interference colors. Biotite: strong pleochroism, bird's eye extinction
Both minerals appear absolutely identical in every optical property when studied under the microscope
Differentiation based only on refractive index measurement
Birefringence values alone distinguish the two minerals
solution: Chlorite: lower birefringence, green/brown. Biotite: high birefringence, strong absorption.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: How does a fill terrace, cut into alluvium, differ from a strath terrace cut into bedrock with thin alluvial cover?
options: Fill and strath terraces are the same type of feature with no difference
Both fill and strath terraces are always formed in alluvial deposits of the river
Fill: in alluvium. Strath: bedrock terrace with thin alluvial cover
Both fill and strath terraces are always cut directly into bedrock
solution: Fill terrace: former floodplain now abandoned. Strath terrace: lateral planation surface.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which remote sensing technique records hundreds of narrow contiguous bands and enables mineral identification by spectral signatures?
options: A few broad bands only, which cannot resolve the narrow absorption features at all
A single panchromatic band, which offers a very high spatial resolution only
100s of narrow bands. Spectral signature identification of minerals
Broad multispectral bands, which are used only for general land cover mapping work
solution: Hyperspectral: AVIRIS, Hyperion, PRISMA, EnMAP. Mineral mapping (clay, iron, carbonate).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Why is quick clay considered extremely hazardous when disturbed?
options: A stiff cemented clay that permanently gains strength when it is disturbed by any loading
Thixotropic clay (high sensitivity). If disturbed, loses strength → flow failure
A clay with sensitivity below 2 that is always fully stable and strong
A clay that cannot flow even under very high pore water pressure
solution: Quick clay: marine clay, leached to low salinity. Sensitivity > 30. Liquefaction flow slides.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which ultramafic rock of olivine and pyroxene represents mantle composition?
options: Granitic plutonic rock rich in quartz, K-feldspar and biotite
Ultramafic rock (olivine + pyroxene). Mantle composition
Dioritic rock composed of plagioclase, hornblende and minor quartz
Syenitic rock consisting mainly of alkali feldspar with little quartz
solution: Peridotite: >90% mafic minerals. Source rock for basaltic magmas.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which formal stratigraphic formations are recognised within the Deccan Traps sequence?
options: Single lava flow that erupted in one continuous event over the entire craton
Two formations separated by a single regional unconformity throughout the pile
Formations: Jawhar, Igatpuri, Neral, Thakurwadi, Bhimashankar, Khandala, etc.
Ten formations of equal thickness with identical geochemical signatures in all flows
solution: Deccan: ~3500m thick in Western Ghats. Twelve formations in Wai Subgroup. Intertrappean beds.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: What is the primary composition and origin of the sedimentary rock limestone?
options: CaCO3 (calcite) — biochemical or chemical
CaMg(CO3)2 — formed by replacement of limestone during diagenesis
SiO2 — chemical precipitate of silica in deep marine basins
Fe2O3 — iron oxide precipitated in oxidizing continental environments
solution: Limestone: fossiliferous, chalk, coquina, oolitic. Effervesces in HCl.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Gneissic banding refers to which textural feature in high-grade metamorphic rocks?
options: Alignment of platy mica minerals along parallel planes
Alternating light (felsic) and dark (mafic) mineral layers
Random orientation of mineral grains without any layering
Lineation defined by elongate minerals parallel to the fold axis
solution: Gneiss: high grade. Segregation into bands. Compositional layering.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which statement about the Moho is correct?
options: It separates the outer core from the mantle and generates the geomagnetic field
It separates the crust from the mantle and shows a velocity increase
It lies within the crust at the depth where temperature exceeds the Curie point
It is a boundary inside the mantle across which seismic velocity drops
solution: The Mohorovičić discontinuity marks the crust–mantle boundary, where P-wave velocity jumps.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Banded iron formations, the main source of iron ore, are characterized by which features and types?
options: Phanerozoic in age, being restricted largely to the Mesozoic coal-bearing basins of Gondwana
Cretaceous in age, formed in shallow Cretaceous epicontinental seas
Tertiary in age, linked to Cenozoic uplift and laterite development
Main Fe ore. Hematite + magnetite. Precambrian. Superior and Algoma types
solution: BIF: iron precipitated from seawater. Oxygenation by cyanobacteria. Major Fe reserve.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A dipping coal seam outcrops over a horizontal width of 100 m on flat ground and dips at 35°. Its true thickness is about:
solution: True thickness = horizontal width × sin(dip) = 100×sin35° ≈ 57.36 m.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: The general three-dimensional groundwater flow equation reduces to Laplace's equation under which condition?
options: Darcy's law applied only to horizontal flow, with no variation in head or velocity across space
∂/∂x(K_x·∂h/∂x) + ∂/∂y(K_y·∂h/∂y) + ∂/∂z(K_z·∂h/∂z) = S_s·∂h/∂t. Laplace: steady
Steady state conditions require that the storage term in the groundwater flow equation be zero
Transient groundwater flow ignores the storage term and assumes a constant hydraulic conductivity everywhere
solution: Steady: ∂²h/∂x² + ∂²h/∂y² + ∂²h/∂z² = 0 (Laplace). Transient: diffusion equation.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Tilted trees, displaced walls and bent fence posts are commonly cited field evidence for which slow mass-wasting process?
options: Tilted trees (pistol-butt), displaced walls, bent fence posts
Lateral shifting of a river channel across its floodplain over time
Curved scars left by rapid downslope movement of material
Deepening of a river bed by vertical downcutting
solution: Creep: slow downslope movement. Indicators: tilted trees, curved soil profiles, displaced objects.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: What determines whether a rock can be ripped or must be blasted?
options: Seismic velocity (Vp) determines ripping vs blasting. Vp < 1500 m/s: easy rip
Rippability depends only on the density of the intact rock material and nothing else
All rocks above Vp of 3000 m/s can still be ripped by heavy dozers
Grain size alone decides whether ripping or blasting is required
solution: Rippability: Caterpillar chart. Vp (m/s): easy <1500, marginal 1500-2000, hard >2000 → blast.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: What is the age, basin setting, and characteristic fossil content of the Siwalik Group?
options: Marine fossils of open-ocean foraminifera deposited in a deep-water shelf setting
Miocene-Pleistocene. Himalayan foreland basin. Fossils: mammals (elephant, horse, ape)
Only volcanic rocks with thick andesitic lava flows and tuff horizons throughout the section
No fossils of any kind due to complete oxidation of the original organic material
solution: Siwalik: sandstone, conglomerate. Himalayan uplift record. Ramapithecus, Sivapithecus.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A P-wave travels at 8 km/s and arrives 10 s after the earthquake. The (approx.) distance to the source is:
options: 80 km
40 km
10 km
0.8 km
solution: distance = velocity × time = 8×10 = 80 km.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: An aquifer (K = 10 m/day) of cross-section 100 m² has a hydraulic gradient of 0.02. The groundwater discharge is about:
options: 1000 m³/day
20 m³/day
10 m³/day
40 m³/day

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: What is the active layer above permafrost, and on what does its depth depend?
options: A permanently frozen zone that never thaws even during the warm summer months of the year
The frozen crust that lies below the permafrost table at depth
A zone of deep thaw that remains unfrozen throughout the year
Seasonal thaw layer above permafrost. Depth: 0.5-5m depending on climate
solution: Active layer: thaws in summer, refreezes in winter. Frost heave. Pile foundations for structures.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Exfoliation (sheeting) joints are curved fractures parallel to the topographic surface that form mainly due to which process?
options: Planar joints formed by regional tectonic compression in massive bedrock
Horizontal joints in sedimentary beds produced during lithification and dewatering
Vertical cooling joints in basaltic lava flows formed during contraction
Curved joints parallel to topographic surface. Unloading (erosion)
solution: Exfoliation: formation of sheet joints. Onion-like weathering. Granite domes (Half Dome).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which regions of the electromagnetic spectrum, from visible through near-infrared to microwave, are used in remote sensing?
options: Only the visible and near-infrared portions of the spectrum
Only thermal infrared, used for temperature measurement
Visible (0.4-0.7 μm), NIR, SWIR, TIR, Microwave (radar)
Only microwave, which cannot sense optical properties
solution: Multispectral: multiple bands. Hyperspectral: hundreds of narrow bands.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: In fold classification, what are the key geometric elements (hinge, limb, axial plane, plunge) that define an anticline or syncline?
options: Anticline is a downfold and syncline is an upfold, named by their relative depth
Anticline (upfold), Syncline (downfold). Hinge, limb, axial plane, plunge
Both fold types are geometrically identical and differ only in their orientation
Folds are classified solely by their wavelength and never by their shape or age
solution: Anticline: oldest in core. Syncline: youngest in core.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Thermal infrared remote sensing measures:
options: Surface temperature and emissivity
Vegetation health through chlorophyll content
Soil moisture in the root zone directly
Water depth through penetration of the column
solution: TIR: 8-14 um wavelength. Detects emitted thermal radiation.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which of the following correctly describes solifluction and the alternative name by which the process is known?
options: Rapid free fall of rock fragments from a steep cliff face to the base of the slope
Fast-moving flow of water-saturated material down a steep slope in a short time
Downslope movement of dry granular material under the influence of gravity with no water involved
Slow downslope flow of water-saturated soil over permafrost. Gelifluction
solution: Solifluction: lobes, sheets. 1-10 cm/yr. Gelifluction: thaw of ice lenses. Terrace-like landforms.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: From a digital elevation model, how are slope and aspect each defined in terms of elevation change?
options: Slope = max rate of change. Aspect = direction of max slope (0-360°)
Slope is the elevation value; aspect is the total relief of the area
Aspect is expressed in metres above mean sea level
Both are derived from land cover, not from elevation
solution: Slope: degrees or %. Derived from DEM (3×3 window, e.g., Horn algorithm). Aspect: N, S, E, W.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which statement about mining method selection is correct?
options: A high stripping ratio favours opencast mining of the shallow seam
A high stripping ratio favours underground over opencast mining
Deep seams are always worked by opencast extraction methods
Stripping ratio has no bearing on the method of selection at all
solution: When too much overburden must be removed per tonne (high stripping ratio), underground mining is preferred.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: An opencast block of 10000 m² has 30 m of overburden above the seam. The overburden volume to be removed is:
options: 0.2 million m³
0.3 million m³
0.6 million m³
0 million m³
solution: Volume = area × depth = 10000×30 = 300000 m³ = 0.3 million m³.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which liquid is commonly used in heavy mineral separation for provenance studies?
options: Bromoform (SG=2.89) separates light from heavy minerals
Magnetic separation using a Frantz isodynamic separator
Optical sorting of grains under plane-polarized light
Chemical dissolution followed by gravimetric measurement
solution: Heavy minerals: SG>2.89. Zircon, tourmaline, rutile (ultra-stable). Garnet, staurolite, kyanite.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Cooper-Jacob straight-line method: drawdown s vs log(t) plot slope:
options: Slope = 2.3Q/T measured over one log cycle
Slope = Q/T for the early part of the data
Slope = Q/(2πT) for the steady state of flow
Slope = 2.3Q/(4πT) for late-time data
solution: Cooper-Jacob: valid for small u (<0.01). Slope Δs over one log cycle = 2.3Q/(4πT).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A coal sample (proximate analysis) has 4% moisture, 20% volatile matter and 8% ash. Its fixed carbon is:
solution: Fixed C = 100 − (moisture + VM + ash) = 100 − (4+20+8) = 68%.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: In a strike-slip fault, displacement is horizontal; what distinguishes a left-lateral fault from a right-lateral fault?
options: Horizontal displacement. Left-lateral vs right-lateral
Vertical displacement where the hanging wall drops down relative to the footwall
Oblique slip with equal horizontal and vertical displacement components
Rotation of blocks about a vertical axis without any horizontal translation
solution: Strike-slip: San Andreas Fault. Transform plate boundary.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Garnet, a common metamorphic mineral, belongs to which crystal system?
options: Hexagonal system
Triclinic system
Cubic (isometric)
Tetragonal system
solution: Garnet: dodecahedral or trapezohedral crystals. Used as abrasive.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: An aquifer (K = 10 m/day) of cross-section 500 m² has a hydraulic gradient of 0.01. The groundwater discharge is about:
options: 5000 m³/day
100 m³/day
50 m³/day
25 m³/day

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which of the following correctly represents the general chemical formula of the mineral tourmaline?
options: (Ca,K,Na,□)(Li,Mg,Fe²⁺,Mn²⁺,Al)₃(Al,Cr,Fe³⁺,V)₆(BO₃)₃Si₆O₁₈(OH)₄
Ca₅(PO₄)₃(F,OH,Cl) — calcium phosphate with fluorine
K(Mg,Fe)₃AlSi₃O₁₀(OH)₂ — hydrous aluminosilicate of the mica group
Mg₃(Si₄O₁₀)(OH)₂ — hydrated magnesium sheet silicate
solution: Tourmaline: complex borosilicate. Wide solid solution. Schorl (Fe), elbaite (Li,Na), dravite (Mg).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: P-T path determination from garnet zoning and inclusions:
options: Garnet core = early P-T. Rim = peak conditions. Inclusions record path
Garnet rims record the earliest conditions of metamorphism
Inclusions are younger than the host garnet and record late events
Only the bulk composition of the whole rock is ever required for the analysis
solution: Garnet: chronometer. Inclusion assemblages at different distances from core = different P-T. Thermobarometry.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: When a competent layer is stretched between incompetent rocks during deformation, what is the resulting pinch-and-swell structure called?
options: Pinch-and-swell structure formed in an incompetent layer squeezed between competent beds
Fold structure produced by vertical buckling of alternating competent and incompetent strata
Boudin (barrel-shaped) structure in competent layer stretched in incompetent matrix
A type of unconformity formed where competent beds are truncated by erosion at the surface
solution: Boudinage: competent layer (quartzite) boudins in incompetent matrix (schist). Necking.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A coal sample (proximate analysis) has 4% moisture, 20% volatile matter and 15% ash. Its fixed carbon is:
solution: Fixed C = 100 − (moisture + VM + ash) = 100 − (4+20+15) = 61%.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: To which structural group of silicate minerals does biotite belong?
options: Tectosilicates (framework silicate minerals)
Inosilicates (chain silicate mineral group)
Phyllosilicates (sheet silicates — micas)
Cyclosilicates (ring silicate mineral group)
solution: Biotite — black mica. One perfect basal cleavage. Common in granite.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: In GIS-based hydrological modeling, what processing of a DEM is required to derive flow accumulation, stream networks, and watersheds?
options: Flow accumulation and watershed delineation can be run on an unfilled DEM directly
Stream network extraction requires only slope; sink filling is optional preprocessing
Flow accumulation, stream network, watershed delineation. Sink filling required
Watershed boundaries are derived from aspect alone, without flow direction grids
solution: DEM → fill sinks → flow direction (D8) → flow accumulation → stream threshold → watershed.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A coal sample (proximate analysis) has 10% moisture, 20% volatile matter and 10% ash. Its fixed carbon is:

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A coal sample (proximate analysis) has 8% moisture, 30% volatile matter and 15% ash. Its fixed carbon is:
solution: Fixed C = 100 − (moisture + VM + ash) = 100 − (8+30+15) = 47%.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Mylonite, a foliated rock from ductile shear zones, forms chiefly by which process?
options: Coarse-grained rock formed by static recrystallization under heat alone without deformation
Brecciated rock containing angular clasts produced by brittle faulting without any subsequent recrystallization or melting
Impact melt glass formed by frictional heating during a large meteorite impact event
Fine-grained, foliated rock in ductile shear zone. Grain size reduction by dynamic recrystallization
solution: Mylonite: ductile deformation. Porphyroclasts in fine matrix. S-C fabrics. Protomylonite→mylonite→ultramylonite.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: An opencast block of 10000 m² has 50 m of overburden above the seam. The overburden volume to be removed is:
options: 0.3 million m³
0 million m³
0.5 million m³
1 million m³
solution: Volume = area × depth = 10000×50 = 500000 m³ = 0.5 million m³.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: To extract 5 m³ of coal, 45 m³ of overburden must be removed. The stripping ratio is:
solution: Stripping ratio = overburden/coal = 45/5 = 9 : 1.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: In a fluvial meandering facies model, channel and floodplain deposits together produce a vertical profile that shows what trend?
options: Alluvial fan with debris flows, sheetfloods and sieve deposits at the mountain front, fining basinward
Delta with mouth bars, distributary channels and prodelta muds
Channel (lag + lateral accretion) + floodplain (levee + crevasse splay + swamp). Vertically fining
Braided alluvium with stacked gravel sheets and minor overbank fines
solution: Meandering: point bar (epsilon cross-bedding). Lateral accretion surfaces (LAS). Mud plug.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: An aquifer has hydraulic conductivity 50 m/day and a hydraulic gradient of 0.05. The Darcy velocity is:
options: 2.5 m/day
5 m/day
50 m/day
1000 m/day

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which option correctly describes a barrier island, its lagoon and the inlets that cut through it?
options: Island of resistant bedrock rising steeply above the sea surface offshore from the coast
Island built by volcanic eruptions on the sea floor near the coastline of the mainland
Long, narrow sand island parallel to coast. Lagoon behind. Inlet cuts
Sand ridge attached to the mainland coast at one of its two ends
solution: Barrier: wave-dominated. Dune ridge, beach, washover fans. Sea-level rise → barrier transgression.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Foliation (planar fabric) is a feature of which rock type?
options: All igneous rocks without exception
All sedimentary rocks
Many metamorphic rocks
Only volcanic tuffs
solution: Directed pressure aligns minerals into foliation in metamorphic rocks like schist and gneiss.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: What is the approximate specific gravity value of the common mineral quartz?
solution: Quartz SG ~2.65. Heavy minerals have SG > 2.85.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A buried erosion surface separating older from much younger rocks is a(n):
options: Plane of maximum curvature along the crest of an anticlinal fold
Unconformity
Surface of continuous deposition with no gap in the geologic record
Fracture along which displacement has occurred between the two blocks
solution: An unconformity represents a gap (missing time) in the rock record.
